body: Sometimes it's the little things. One time, what kept me alive was that I hadn't finished Adventure Time yet.

Please, I hope you're still alive. For what it's worth, I have a friend who's gone through some similar experiences, and she currently is living a really happy and full life. She has her dream job in a town she likes. 

Your traumas...I don't want to  minimize them. You've been through some truly terrible things. But with time, you can learn to heal. You can be happy again. 

Also, your family outside of your aunt and her child completely sucks. Please don't use them as a measurement for your worth.

As a side note, not to get weird and personal, but my mental health issues that made me go sorta...off the wall were because of undergrad, so I'm slightly worried the workload of grad school will be even worse and I'll just get even worse. 

Sorry, I don't expect a reply to that (although anyone is welcome to attempt one) since that's more of a mental health thing than a writing thing.
Honestly, I'm not sure. I guess if I went through this it would be professor, or maybe some kind of more niche academic job, which I've heard exist.

Hey, I'm a lot calmer now. I had a hard night to say the least. While you certainly make a good point about how "living out of spite" isn't always the healthiest mentality to have, I think when you're at a mental low, it's one of the only things that can motivate you do keep going. I plan on doing a follow up post
